claims.claim_text: The indexed Merle R Shuster is a high-confidence match to the official Army bulk file.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact full name and a nonshared protected identifier agree across the OSS index and official Army record.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from exact name and nonshared protected identifier.
claims.temporal_assessment: The Army record establishes wartime identity, not a named pre-OSS employer or precise OSS-entry sequence.

claims.claim_text: The official Army candidate conflicts with the indexed given name Emily L Shwetzer and is not accepted as the same person.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Doosik Shynn is probably the Korean-American editor and activist documented as Doo Sik Shynn.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The uncommon name and its documented transliterations agree, but an accessible personnel-file bridge has not yet been found.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Probable from the uncommon name, transliteration variants, period and Korean-American context; Box 708 remains necessary for confirmation.
claims.temporal_assessment: The scholarly source documents the person in 1938, several years before OSS service, but does not establish the intervening sequence.
claims.match_notes: The claim is visibly qualified and excluded from confirmed/high default identity analytics.

claims.claim_text: A scholarly study identifies Doo Sik Shynn as editor in chief of The New Korea in 1938.

claims.temporal_assessment: Documented in 1938, before OSS, but not shown to be the immediate pre-OSS affiliation or last civilian employer.
claims.match_notes: The role is published as a qualified documented-prewar job, not as an immediate predecessor to OSS.
